t: Champa was less a single kingdom than a confederation of Cham principalities along the coast, Indrapura, Amaravati, Vijaya, Kauthara and Panduranga, united by language and culture, with a king of kings in some periods.
Between the 7th and 10th centuries Cham fleets controlled the spice and silk trade of the South China Sea, and eaglewood from the highlands was the kingdom's chief export.
The Vietnamese conquest of Vijaya in 1471, in which 120,000 people were killed or captured, reduced Champa to Kauthara and Panduranga; Panduranga was annexed by Minh Mạng in 1832.
dyk: The Đông Yên Châu inscription, found in Champa and dated to around 350 CE, is the oldest known text written in a native Southeast Asian language, centuries before the first Khmer, Mon or Malay texts.
ev: Khu Liên, an official at Xianglin, rebels against the Eastern Han dynasty and founds Lâm Ấp, the predecessor state of Champa.
Bhadravarman, the first king acknowledged in the inscriptions, establishes the linga Bhadresvara at Mỹ Sơn.
The Sui Empire invades Lâm Ấp, overruns Sambhuvarman's resistance and sacks the capital at Trà Kiệu.
Indravarman II founds Indrapura and a Buddhist dynasty; the years to 982 are called the Golden Age of Champa art.
Jaya Indravarman IV's fleet takes Angkor by surprise, kills the Khmer king and begins a four-year Cham occupation of Cambodia.
The Yuan army under Sogetu takes Vijaya; Indravarman V and Prince Harijit wage a two-year guerrilla war and drive the Mongols out.
Lê Thánh Tông's army destroys Vijaya; 120,000 Cham are killed or captured and the kingdom shrinks to Kauthara and Panduranga.
Minh Mạng arrests the last king, Po Phaok The, and annexes Panduranga as the provinces of Ninh Thuận and Bình Thuận.

f.capital: Simhapura (Trà Kiệu); Indrapura (Đồng Dương) from about 875; Vijaya (Cha Ban) from the 1150s to 1471; then Panduranga (Phan Rang)
f.founder: Khu Liên (Ou Lian), an official of the Eastern Han who rebelled at Xianglin in 192 and founded Lâm Ấp
f.predecessor: The Sa Huỳnh culture and Lâm Ấp (Linyi), the rebel state in the Han commandery of Xianglin
f.successor: The Nguyễn dynasty of Vietnam, which made Panduranga the provinces of Ninh Thuận and Bình Thuận
